axes.name: popcount
axes.definition: number of 1 entries in the 128-entry rule table
axes.basis: quartiles of Binomial(128, 1/2): equal mass for a uniformly random table

axes.name: centre1_ones
axes.definition: number of 1 outputs among the 64 neighbourhoods whose centre cell is 1

grid: 4 x 4 = 16 cells; a uniformly random table has probability ~1/16 per cell by construction
purpose: to separate the ACQUISITION ARM (random tables) into equal-mass cells so every retention policy faces occupancy across the whole grid, not 4 of 16 cells; v0's equal-WIDTH bins put 120 random rules in 4 cells because popcount concentrates at 64 +- 6 (Techne's measurement). This is a descriptor of the TABLE, never of the outcome; historical genomes and constants land where their tables put them (constants at the corners: popcount 0 or 128).
what_it_does_not_do: it does not separate rules by behaviour; two tables in one cell may compute very different things. A behavioural descriptor is a different experiment and would need the C3-3 criterion first.
replaces: h3_replay v0 edges ((0.25,0.5,0.75),(0.25,0.5,0.75)) on normalised popcount / centre1 counts
